title: How many fractions can we find that are equivalent to four sixths?
description: Four sixths is divided on the top and the bottom by two, and the result is multiplied by three, four and five on the top and the bottom. The list of fractions is checked by taking two thirds of each bottom number.
teaching_notes: One idea: one fraction gives a whole list of equivalent fractions when the top and the bottom are multiplied by the same number. Watch for students who stop after the first fraction they find.

source: Figure it Out Q3 (section 7.6, first block)
video_script.why: A learner writes a list of fractions equivalent to four sixths by dividing and multiplying the top and the bottom by the same number.
video_script.substitution: none: the book's own fraction four sixths
video_script.anchor: a paper strip cut into six equal parts with four parts shaded, and a row of empty boxes joined by equals signs
video_script.payoff_line: Fractions equivalent to four sixths are two thirds, six ninths, eight twelfths and ten fifteenths

final_answer.spoken: two thirds, six ninths, eight twelfths, ten fifteenths and more

video_script.fraction_reading: four sixths, two thirds, six ninths, eight twelfths, ten fifteenths
maths_rules: divide the top and the bottom of 4/6 by 2: (4 ÷ 2)/(6 ÷ 2) = 2/3
multiply 2/3 by 3 on top and bottom: (2 × 3)/(3 × 3) = 6/9
check: in each of 4/6, 2/3, 6/9, 8/12, 10/15 the top number is two thirds of the bottom number
video_script.design: One idea: do the same thing to the top and the bottom, again and again. The strip stays on the board and a row of boxes fills up beside it.

beats.on_screen: small title card From your book; a paper strip cut into 6 equal parts with 4 parts shaded, and a row of empty boxes beside it

marks.scene: the title card and the strip appear
marks.row: a row of empty boxes appears beside the strip
marks.ask: the words as many as you can appear

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about four sixths of a strip.
<bookmark mark='row'/>We fill the boxes with fractions that are equivalent to four sixths.

beats.on_screen: the strip and the row of boxes stay on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

beats.on_screen: the strip with 4 of 6 parts shaded; the parts are joined in pairs into 3 parts, and also cut into more slices, while the shaded length stays the same

marks.join: the six parts join in pairs into three bigger parts, with two of them shaded
marks.cut: each part is cut into more slices, and the shaded length stays the same

narration: <bookmark mark='join'/>Joining the parts in pairs makes fewer, bigger parts, and the shaded length stays the same.
<bookmark mark='cut'/>Cutting every part into more slices makes more, smaller parts, and the shaded length still stays the same.

beats.on_screen: To find: as many fractions equivalent to 4/6 as we can

marks.find: the question to find is written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find as many fractions equivalent to four sixths as we can.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: divide the top and the bottom of 4/6 by 2: (4 ÷ 2)/(6 ÷ 2) gives 2/3

marks.top: an arrow marked ÷ 2 joins the 4 to a 2
marks.bottom: an arrow marked ÷ 2 joins the 6 to a 3

narration: <bookmark mark='top'/>Step one, divide the top and the bottom of four sixths by two, because two divides both numbers.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: multiply the top and the bottom of 2/3 by 3: (2 × 3)/(3 × 3) gives 6/9

marks.times: an arrow marked × 3 joins the 2 to a 6 and the 3 to a 9

narration: <bookmark mark='times'/>Step two, multiply the top and the bottom of two thirds by three, as in your book. We get six ninths.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: multiply 2/3 by 4 on top and bottom to get 8/12; by 5 to get 10/15
narration: <bookmark mark='four'/>Step three, multiply two thirds by four on top and bottom to get eight twelfths.
<bookmark mark='five'/>Multiply by five to get ten fifteenths, and we can go on.

beats.on_screen: Check: two thirds of each bottom number gives its top number: 6 gives 4, 3 gives 2, 9 gives 6, 12 gives 8, 15 gives 10

marks.check: two thirds of each bottom number is taken and matches the top number

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>To check, take two thirds of each bottom number. It must give the top number.

marks.pay: the chain of equal fractions is written and boxed

narration: <bookmark mark='pay'/>Fractions equivalent to four sixths are two thirds, six ninths, eight twelfths and ten fifteenths.
The list can go on and on.
